crossing supervisor Listen Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print Content components School crossing supervisors have a much-valued role in Boroondara. On an average school day in Boroondara, they help 9,266 pedestrians to cross the street while 74,426 motor vehicles use our roads during school crossing times. We are always looking for school crossing supervisors. If you are friendly, reliable and flexible, this role is for you. What does a school crossing supervisor do? This paid position gives you the opportunity to get involved in your community and improve road safety for children, people with a disability and the general public who use our 114 school crossings. School crossing supervisors: • work part-time Monday to Friday, from 8 am to 9 am and from 3 pm to 4 pm, during the school term • play an important role in educating children with ‘Stop, Look and Listen’ instructions • are responsible for reporting any road hazards or potential risks • help to encourage active and independent travel. About you We are looking for people aged 18 and older who: • can attend shifts at short notice • have their own reliable transport • are able to work across several locations • can complete the pre-employment medical and police checks. You will have access to a full training program before starting your role. Submit an online application through our Careers website . Attend an interview – meet with one of our Council Officers at Council, located at 8 Inglesby Road in Camberwell. Provide us with relevant employment documents – including your Working With Children Check, Police Check and evidence of your COVID-19 vaccination status. Complete a medical assessment. Apply to become a School Crossings Supervisor We are always recruiting new school crossing supervisors to help people to cross our roads safely at peak school times. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Senior Test Lead (15184) Requisition ID 15184 - Posted - Job Function (1) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List Senior Test Lead - Enterprise Transformation Lead quality, testing and implementation readiness for a major Council transformation Own the Council-side testing strategy across SaaS implementation, integrations, data migration and business acceptance Full-time limited tenure role until 31 August 2027 | Camberwell | Hybrid working | $136,121-$152,407 plus super and RDO A little bit about the role City of Boroondara is transforming how property, planning, permitting and other essential Council services are delivered to the community. We are seeking an accomplished Senior Test Lead to establish and lead the Council-side quality and testing function through configuration, integration, data migration, business acceptance and implementation readiness. The Senior Test Lead will provide specialist quality and testing leadership for the Property, Planning and Permits project and the broader Transform Boroondara Program. This is a hands-on leadership role with the authority to establish the Council-side testing approach, coordinate multidisciplinary Council and supplier resources, challenge the quality of delivery evidence and provide clear recommendations to senior governance forums on implementation readiness. You will establish and govern a risk-based testing approach, lead end-to-end testing and business acceptance, and coordinate targeted assurance across critical business processes, data, integrations and controls. You will also help establish sustainable testing, regression and continuous assurance practices that Council can use to manage future SaaS releases. Working closely with business sponsors, ICT, delivery partners and specialist assurance providers, you will ensure solutions are fit for purpose, compliant, reliable and ready to implement. The role will interpret the Program Quality and Testing Standards and develop the procedures, evidence requirements and controls needed to apply them. It will direct Council-side testing across system configuration, integrations, data migration, critical business journeys, financial and regulatory controls, cutover and operational readiness. You will work with employees at all levels across Council and lead multidisciplinary resources from Council, delivery partners and specialist assurance providers. Key responsibilities include: Establish and govern the quality and testing approach for the Property, Planning and Permits project and the broader Transform Boroondara Program. Lead system integration testing, end-to-end testing, business acceptance, defect management and implementation-readiness assessment. Establish clear traceability between business requirements, risks, test coverage, results, defects and acceptance decisions. Coordinate targeted assurance across financial controls, data integrity, migration, compliance, privacy, security and operational readiness. Critically assess supplier test plans, results and supporting evidence, ensuring Council has sufficient independent evidence to make informed implementation decisions. Lead and coordinate multidisciplinary Council, supplier and specialist assurance resources across concurrent workstreams. Provide authoritative advice to senior stakeholders, business owners and governance forums on quality risks, readiness and conditions for acceptance. Establish a proportionate automation and regression approach that can be sustained by Council following implementation. Support the development of stronger testing and continuous assurance capability across Council. A little bit about you You are an accomplished quality and testing leader with substantial experience delivering complex SaaS, ERP or enterprise-system implementations. You have personally led testing across integrations, data migration, end-to-end business processes and business acceptance, rather than only coordinating test activity or reporting progress. You bring strong knowledge of risk-based testing, test governance, traceability, evidence management, defect management, automation and implementation readiness. You are comfortable challenging delivery partners, identifying gaps in testing evidence and providing clear, independent advice to senior stakeholders and governance forums. You will have strong analytical, interpersonal and communication skills, with demonstrated ability to: Establish and lead testing within complex, supplier-led delivery environments. Coordinate business, technical, supplier and specialist-assurance resources. Translate complex technical, financial and operational evidence into clear recommendations. Negotiate priorities and resolve issues across multiple delivery workstreams. Balance strategic test leadership with direct, hands-on involvement in plans, evidence, risks and decisions. Experience with local government, regulatory services, financial controls or revenue-related systems will be well regarded. A relevant tertiary qualification, or equivalent specialist training and experience, is required. ISTQB Advanced Test Manager certification, or an equivalent qualification, is highly desirable. Why join us? This is an opportunity to: Shape the quality and testing approach for a significant enterprise transformation. Work with direct access to senior business owners, program leadership and governance forums. Influence critical implementation decisions and supplier performance. Establish practical testing and assurance capabilities that will remain with Council after implementation. Contribute to improving how essential Council services are delivered to the Boroondara community. Join a funded full-time appointment covering the program’s critical configuration, testing and implementation-readiness period. Want to know more You can connect further and gain a better insight into this opportunity by reviewing the Position Description . Employment requirements Applicants must have the right to work in Australia Preferred applicants will be required to undergo a National Police Record Check How to apply If you are ready to work in a senior specialist role with strong stakeholder visibility, influencing release readiness, risk decisions and supplier performance, we would love to hear from you. Please submit your application online via the ‘ Apply’ button. All applications must be made via the online portal by Thursday 3 September at 11.59pm . No applications direct to the hiring manager or from recruitment agencies will be considered. Applications may be reviewed as they are received. If you want to know more about the benefits of working for the City of Boroondara, please visit our careers website borooondara.vic.gov/careers Council recognises the benefits of a diverse workforce for its employees and customers. To ensure equity of access to employment opportunities, Council encourages applications from underrepresented groups including people who are from an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander background, people from different ages, abilities, gender identities, sexual orientation and cultural backgrounds. If you require any additional support or adjustments regarding interview arrangements, please advise the contact listed above in advance. Council is a child safe organisation and as such, some applicants may be required to hold a Working with Children Check. We understand that this portal may not meet the needs of people who rely on Assistive Technology or have other diverse requirements. If you have any difficulty using our recruitment system, please do not hesitate to contact People Culture and Development on (03) 9278 4401 or pcd@boroondara.vic.gov.au to allow us to help in any way we can. Who are we? The City of Boroondara is a metropolitan council, representing more than 170,000 people in the inner-eastern suburbs of Melbourne. A leader in the local government sector, with a reputation for innovation and excellence, we believe in providing an environment where our staff thrive, both in the work they do and in how they learn and develop as people and professionals. We like to challenge the norm and we are investing significantly in innovation and technology improvements in order to provide our customers with an even greater experience and engagement. We are putting our customers at the forefront of what we do with our organisation wide initiative, Transforming Boroondara Program. You will be instrumental in driving this change across the organisation using best practice approaches to successfully support us from the now to our desired future state. A little bit about the role The Customer Connect team prides itself on playing a front facing role in line with the customer Experience Improvement Strategy to achieve exceptionally high customer satisfaction. The Quality and Training Officer works collaboratively with Customer Connect, the Customer Operations Team and employees across Council to strengthen service capability and support the delivery of an exceptional customer experience. In this multi-skilled role, the Quality and Training Officer will review and monitor customer interactions and feedback to identify coaching, training and improvement opportunities. This key role will develop and deliver training modules, undertake quality evaluations in line with the Customer Connect Quality Framework, and help maintain accurate and reliable knowledge management content. Key responsibilities include: Conducting quality evaluations in line with the Customer Connect Quality Framework. Identifying coaching and training opportunities through customer interactions, feedback and quality review processes. Developing, coordinating and delivering engaging face-to-face and virtual training for Customer Connect and wider Council audiences. Supporting continuous improvement initiatives that enhance customer satisfaction and service consistency. Maintaining knowledge management content to ensure information is accessible, reliable and up to date. Working professionally with internal and external stakeholders, including consultants, vendors and service providers where required. A little bit about you You will have contemporary contact centre experience, strong communication skills and a practical understanding of quality, training and knowledge management practices. You will be confident in engaging with diverse stakeholders, sharing knowledge, providing objective feedback and tailoring training materials to suit different audiences. To be successful in this role, you will have: Demonstrated experience developing, coordinating and delivering training in a contemporary contact centre environment, face to face and virtually A working knowledge of Agile methodologies preferably in the context of a Contact Centre. Demonstrated ability to build capability by coaching, educating and sharing knowledge with others. Strong planning, prioritisation and self-management skills, with the ability to manage competing demands. Sound judgement, initiative and resourcefulness, with the ability to work effectively as part of multidisciplinary teams. Experience using customer request management systems, knowledge management systems, corporate systems and Microsoft Office applications. Highly developed written and verbal communication skills and a collaborative approach to problem solving. A qualification in training or relevant experience in teaching, training, assessment. Want to know more You can connect further and gain a better insight into this opportunity by reviewing the Position Decription. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Park Asset Specialist (15178) Requisition ID 15178 - Posted - Job Function (2) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List $73,273 to $78,901 (ongoing, full time, plus superannuation, 9 day fortnight) Build and maintain the parks and playgrounds that our community enjoys every day Work outdoors across some of Melbourne's most valued parks and reserves The Role Reporting to the Parks Team Leader, the Park Asset Specialist plays an important role in maintaining the safety, functionality and presentation of Council's playgrounds, park furniture and associated infrastructure. Based at Kew Depot and working across the municipality, this hands-on role is responsible for delivering maintenance and repair services that ensure our parks and open spaces remain safe, attractive and welcoming for the community. You will undertake a variety of maintenance activities, inspections and repair works while working collaboratively with colleagues, contractors and members of the public. Key Responsibilities Carry out maintenance, repairs and minor construction works across playgrounds, park furniture and fence assets within Council's open spaces. Undertake routine playground inspections and audits to ensure compliance with relevant Australian Standards and identify any safety concerns. Arrange for hazards and defects to be repaired, replaced or made safe in a timely manner, ensuring community safety remains a priority. Plan and complete maintenance works while considering the horticultural amenity and presentation of park sites, leaving work areas clean and safe upon completion . About You You will bring practical experience in outdoor maintenance, construction, landscaping, carpentry or a related field, together with a strong commitment to safety and high-quality workmanship. You have experience installing, repairing and maintaining outdoor furniture, structures or timber assets and enjoy working in a physically active outdoor environment. You are self-motivated, organised and capable of managing your workload while responding to changing priorities. Your ability to work both independently and as part of a team, combined with strong communication skills, will enable you to build positive relationships with colleagues and the community. Qualifications or experience in carpentry, landscaping, welding, forklift operation or medium rigid vehicle operation will be highly regarded. For more information regarding the role, please refer to the attached position description. About Boroondara The City of Boroondara is home to some of Melbourne's most beautiful parks, playgrounds, gardens and open spaces. We are committed to creating a healthy, connected and sustainable community and delivering services that place our customers at the centre of everything we do. As one of Melbourne's most desirable municipalities, we take pride in maintaining high quality public spaces that support recreation, wellbeing and community connection. Working with us means contributing to assets and environments that are enjoyed by thousands of residents and visitors each year. Employment Requirements Applicants must hold unrestricted working rights in Australia, and those progressing through the selection process will need to complete a National Police Record Check, a Working with Children Check and relevant pre-employment medical assessments. How to Apply Please submit your application online via the 'Apply' button by 11.59pm, Sunday 23 August 2026. All applications must be made via the online portal; no applications direct to the hiring manager or from recruitment agencies will be considered.
